text:
Marathon Petroleum recovered slightly today, gaining 0.44%, after a sharp two-week pullback of 6.76%. The gain comes as refineries continue running at high capacity (95.2%) and crude prices hold relatively steady in the $89–$92 range, but the broader context is pulling in opposite directions: Russian oil output has rebounded sharply, pushing global supply back into surplus according to the IEA, which typically pressures refiner margins and crude prices.

The spike in heating oil prices (up 59% year-over-year) might seem bullish for a refiner, but it reflects constrained supply and high demand—not the kind of sustained margin expansion refiners see in a balanced market. With Russian production recovering and inventories of diesel at comfortable levels, the near-term tailwind for refined product pricing is fading, which helps explain why the stock sold off over the past fortnight despite strong refinery utilization.
